title: Hollow Verbs (Al-Fiʿl al-Ajwaf)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 28; Ryding Ch. 22 §22.6)
objectives: Identify hollow verbs with middle weak radical و or ي (قَالَ, بَاعَ, خَافَ).
Apply morphophonemic vowel shortening in closed syllables (قُلْتُ, بِعْتُ, لَمْ يَقُلْ).
Distinguish the three hollow stem classes by their imperfect vowel (يَقُولُ, يَبِيعُ, يَخَافُ).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 13: How does كَانَ shorten when ـْتُ attaches (كُنْتُ)?

sections.heading: Middle Weak Radical (Wāw or Yāʾ)
sections.body: Hollow verbs (al-ajwaf) have و or ي as their middle radical. In the 3rd-person past, the weak radical appears as a long alif (قَالَ from ق-و-ل; بَاعَ from ب-ي-ع; خَافَ from خ-و-ف). In the imperfect, the original weak letter or long vowel reappears: يَقُولُ (ū), يَبِيعُ (ī), يَخَافُ (ā).

sections.label: Closed-Syllable Shortening
sections.summary: Arabic forbids a long vowel followed by a vowelless consonant (C̄Cْ). Whenever the 3rd radical takes sukūn—either before consonant suffixes (قُلْتُ, بِعْتُ) or in the jussive/imperative (لَمْ يَقُلْ, قُلْ)—the long medial vowel shortens to its corresponding short vowel (u, i, or a).

sections.translation: He did not say anything except the truth.
sections.irab: لَمْ: حَرْفُ نَفْيٍ وَجَزْمٍ | يَقُلْ: فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ مَجْزُومٌ بِالسُّكُونِ (وَحُذِفَتِ الوَاوُ لِالْتِقَاءِ السَّاكِنَيْنِ)
sections.notes: In يَقُولُ, adding jussive sukūn on ل creates يَقُولْ; the long ū shortens to u → لَمْ يَقُلْ.

sections.heading: Notice What Returns in the Subjunctive
sections.body: In the subjunctive (لَنْ يَقُولَ), the final ل carries fatḥah, so the syllable is open and the long vowel stays: يَقُولَ.
